# Equipment desk

The Eastbank community centre lends individually tagged equipment to registered volunteers.
Desk volunteers hand equipment over and record returns, often while another person waits.
They need to find the right item, see whether it can be lent, and complete the handover without
confusing two people with similar names. They also need to find an outstanding loan when
someone brings an item back.

The desk uses a 1024 by 768 laptop with a mouse and keyboard. Volunteers also use a 390-pixel-wide
phone when collecting returned equipment from another room. There is no scanner. This is an
indoor, light-mode desk tool. Long names must remain identifiable at either size. No visual
identity, component library, prior screen or accepted visual design exists.

The current command-line ledger reads data/equipment.json. The source is in src/ledger.py.
The file contains the actual equipment labels and volunteer names for this proposal. It is a
snapshot for 16 May 2026; closing time is 18:00. EQ-041 is overdue. Keep this ledger available
while we decide on the new screen.

## Lending rules

- Each tag identifies one item. Quantities and multi-item transactions are outside this screen.
- Find equipment by tag or any part of its name, and volunteers by ID or any part of their name.
  Matching ignores case. Show IDs with names so Maya Chen and Maya Chavez are distinguishable.
- Checking out requires one available item and one volunteer from the supplied roster. The due
  time is always 18:00 on the desk date. The volunteer can already have other items on loan.
- Before completing a checkout, the desk volunteer must be able to verify the item, borrower
  and due time. Completing it changes the item to on loan and shows who has it and when it is due.
- An item on loan cannot be checked out again. Maintenance items cannot be lent and must show
  the reason. Availability must be understandable without relying only on color.
- A return identifies an existing loan and makes its item available again. Show the current
  borrower and due time before completing the return. Do not ask for a new borrower on return.
- An overdue loan remains returnable and does not block another checkout. There are no fees,
  renewals, reservations, borrower registration, authentication or damaged-return workflows here.
- Cancelling an unfinished checkout or return changes nothing. Missing required selections
  leave the transaction unfinished with a useful explanation. A search with no matches must
  leave a way to search again or restore the list.

## Open screen choice

Volunteers disagree about where a handover should begin. Some look up the equipment tag first;
others look up the volunteer first and then choose equipment or one of that person's loans.
Both use the lending rules above. We have not selected either starting point or a layout.
The question is which makes the item and borrower easier to verify without slowing returns.

For this proposal, changes can stay in memory and reload can restore the snapshot. The existing
ledger remains the operational record until we choose a screen and authorize integration.
